cases.name: tier_c_grant_admitted
cases.note: A complete grant at the maximum issuable ceiling, signed by the active authority key, covering every declaration the archive's own manifest makes. The tree enumerates entries out of digest order, carries a directory entry the digest ignores, and embeds the grant at the root, which the digest excludes — so admission proves byte ordering, directory handling and grant exclusion at once.

cases.name: verify_only_key_admitted
cases.note: The same payload granted at Tier B — the least ceiling covering the manifest's declarations — by a key the registry has moved to verify_only. Rotation must not invalidate the catalogue.

cases.name: nested_grant_json_counted
cases.note: A file named grant.json below the root. Exclusion is by exact root name, so this file is inside the digest; the grant is issued over that digest and admits.

reject_cases.name: missing_grant_file
reject_cases.note: The archive carries no root grant.json. There is no grant to verify, and no side channel to consult instead; the placement rule refuses the package before anything parses.
reject_cases.reason: no root grant.json in the archive

reject_cases.name: missing_manifest
reject_cases.note: The archive carries no root skill.yaml. Identity and package admission read the authenticated manifest, so its absence refuses before anything parses.
reject_cases.reason: no root skill.yaml in the archive

reject_cases.name: traversal_path
reject_cases.note: A file entry whose path contains a .. segment.
reject_cases.reason: tree path contains a dot segment

reject_cases.name: dir_traversal_path
reject_cases.note: A directory entry whose path contains a .. segment. A directory is ignored by the digest and still validated here: ignored-by-the-digest is not ignored-by-safety.
reject_cases.reason: tree path contains a dot segment

reject_cases.name: absolute_path
reject_cases.note: An entry path beginning with /.

reject_cases.name: empty_path
reject_cases.note: An entry whose path is zero bytes long.

reject_cases.name: nul_path
reject_cases.note: An entry path containing 0x00 — the byte the digest serialisation uses as its separator, which is why it can never appear in a path.

reject_cases.name: invalid_utf8_path
reject_cases.note: An entry path that is not valid UTF-8, representable here because paths travel as raw bytes.
reject_cases.reason: tree path is not valid UTF-8

reject_cases.name: duplicate_tree_path
reject_cases.note: Two archive entries with byte-identical paths. An extracted tree would have collapsed them, which is why enumeration happens on the authenticated archive.

reject_cases.name: dir_duplicate_path
reject_cases.note: A directory entry whose path duplicates the regular skill.yaml. Duplicate detection runs across all entry kinds.

reject_cases.name: backslash_traversal_dir
reject_cases.note: A directory entry whose path is Windows-style traversal. The backslash is forbidden as a byte, so no consumer platform can reinterpret it as a separator; a directory entry keeps the digest unchanged, so archive admission alone decides it.

reject_cases.name: drive_path_dir
reject_cases.note: A directory entry with a drive-qualified Windows path.

reject_cases.name: unc_path_dir
reject_cases.note: A directory entry with a UNC path.

reject_cases.name: empty_segment_dir
reject_cases.note: A directory entry whose path contains an empty segment. a//b and dir/ are aliases that collapse into other paths during extraction.
reject_cases.reason: tree path contains an empty segment

reject_cases.name: trailing_slash_dir
reject_cases.note: A directory entry with a trailing slash — the other empty-segment alias.
reject_cases.reason: tree path contains an empty segment

reject_cases.name: symlink_entry
reject_cases.note: An entry that is neither a regular file nor a directory.

reject_cases.name: unknown_field
reject_cases.note: The embedded grant carries an expires_at field. The grant object is strict.

reject_cases.name: missing_field
reject_cases.note: permitted_actions is absent. Every field is required.

reject_cases.name: duplicate_json_key
reject_cases.note: The embedded grant's raw JSON spells max_tier twice, A then C. A parser that keeps the last duplicate admits a ceiling nobody signed; strict parsing refuses the bytes before any object exists. No canonical bytes are recorded because no parsed object legitimately exists.

reject_cases.name: wrong_schema
reject_cases.note: schema names a version this contract does not define.

reject_cases.name: tier_d_ceiling
reject_cases.note: Correctly signed by the active key, claiming max_tier D. Refused as malformed before the registry or signature is consulted: a correctly signed claim of an unissuable authority is not a signature problem.
reject_cases.reason: max_tier must be A, B, or C

reject_cases.name: bad_digest_format
reject_cases.note: payload_sha256 is not sha256:<64-lowercase-hex>.

reject_cases.name: duplicate_list_entry
reject_cases.note: permitted_triggers lists one name twice.

reject_cases.name: identity_syntax_invalid
reject_cases.note: skill_name begins with a hyphen, which the manifest name syntax forbids. Signed correctly; refused for its content.
reject_cases.reason: skill_name does not satisfy the manifest name syntax

reject_cases.name: identity_overlong
reject_cases.note: skill_name is 65 characters against the manifest's 64-character bound.

reject_cases.name: identity_control_character
reject_cases.note: skill_version carries U+202E, a bidirectional override. Identity fields obey the manifest's identity-field character rules, checked before the registry, the signature, or any binding.
reject_cases.reason: identity field contains a forbidden character

reject_cases.name: unknown_key_id
reject_cases.note: Names a key id absent from the registry. Refused at key resolution, before any signature check, so the reason names the key, not the bytes.
reject_cases.reason: authority_key_id is not in the registry

reject_cases.name: revoked_key
reject_cases.note: Names a registry key with status revoked. Revoked keys fail closed even though the signature they made would still verify mathematically.

reject_cases.name: tampered_ceiling
reject_cases.note: Signed with max_tier B, presented with max_tier C. The ceiling is inside the signed bytes, so the tamper is a signature failure, not a field failure.
reject_cases.reason: signature does not verify over the presented grant

reject_cases.name: bad_signature_encoding
reject_cases.note: The signature value is not base64. Encoding rules are enforced at the signature stage and fail closed.
reject_cases.reason: signature is not valid ed25519 encoding

reject_cases.name: payload_digest_mismatch
reject_cases.note: The admitted Tier C grant over a tree whose hooks.py differs by one line. A valid signature over the wrong payload refuses at payload binding, after the signature verifies.
reject_cases.reason: payload tree digest does not match payload_sha256

reject_cases.name: skill_name_mismatch
reject_cases.note: Issued for another name over this same payload tree; every earlier stage passes, so identity binding against the archive's own manifest alone decides it.
reject_cases.reason: skill_name does not match the manifest name

reject_cases.name: skill_version_mismatch
reject_cases.note: Issued for another version over this same payload tree.
reject_cases.reason: skill_version does not match the manifest version

reject_cases.name: unpermitted_trigger
reject_cases.note: The grant verifies — signature, digest and identity all bind — but permitted_triggers is empty while the archive's manifest declares anomalous_draw. Grant verification is not package admission.

reject_cases.name: unpermitted_action
reject_cases.note: The manifest declares switch_power_source; the grant permits only alert_whatsapp.

reject_cases.name: tier_above_ceiling
reject_cases.note: Every name is permitted, but the manifest declares a Tier B action under a Tier A ceiling.
reject_cases.reason: declared tier B exceeds max_tier A
